name: Asa in his latter years
charge: Hiring the king of Syria against Israel; imprisoning the seer who reproved him; seeking to the physicians and not to the Lord
summary: For thirty-five years Asa was one of Judah's best kings. Then Baasha fortified Ramah, and Asa emptied the temple treasury to buy Ben-hadad's help instead of relying on the Lord who had given him the Ethiopians. Rebuked, he put the seer in the stocks; diseased, he sought physicians; and he died in the forty-first year of his reign.
offense: When Baasha fortified Ramah, Asa took silver and gold from the house of the Lord and the king's house and hired Ben-hadad to break his agreement with Israel. The plan relieved the immediate pressure, but Asa had relied upon the king of Syria instead of the Lord who had delivered him from the Ethiopians. Hanani exposed the difference between a successful maneuver and a faithful heart. Asa answered the rebuke with anger, imprisoned the seer, and oppressed some of the people. Later, when disease afflicted his feet, he sought the physicians but not the Lord. The charge is his neglect of God; the passage does not make the use of physicians itself the offense.
judgment: Hanani declared that the Syrian host had escaped Asa's hand and that he would have wars. Asa had purchased temporary relief while losing the greater deliverance that reliance upon God would have brought. His disease became exceedingly severe, and he died in the forty-first year of his reign. He received an honorable burial, but the honor shown at his death did not erase the rebuke recorded against his latter years. The king who once cried to God against an immense army resisted correction when his own policy was challenged.

entries.commentary: In the six and thirtieth year of Asa, Baasha king of Israel comes up against Judah and builds Ramah to keep any from going out or coming in to Asa. Baasha is trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah, because tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa.

Instead of crying to the Most High as he did against Zerah, Asa takes silver and gold out of the house of the Lord and the king's house and hires Benhadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha. Benhadad smites the cities of Israel, so Baasha leaves off building Ramah. Asa carries away the stones and timber of Ramah and builds Geba and Mizpah with them.

Hanani the seer comes to Asa and rebukes him for relying on the king of Syria and not on the Most High, so the host of Syria has escaped his hand. Had he relied on the Most High, he would have delivered them as he did the Ethiopians. The eyes of the Most High run to and fro throughout the whole earth to show himself strong for them whose heart is perfect. Asa is wroth, puts the seer in prison, and oppresses some of the people.

In the thirty and ninth year of his reign Asa is diseased in his feet, exceeding great, yet he seeks not to the Most High but to the physicians. The rebuke is not against physicians but against seeking them in place of the Most High, from whom healing cometh. Asa dies in the one and fortieth year of his reign and is buried in his own sepulchre in the city of David, on a bed of sweet odours and spices, with a very great burning. -

Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and walks in all the sins of his father, his heart not perfect with the Most High as David's was. The children did what they saw their fathers do, not merely what was said, which is why the Most High teaches His people to be different. Yet for David's sake the Most High gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, because David did right all his days save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite, a wrong from which David repented. -

After Abijam dies, Asa his son reigns forty-one years and does right in the eyes of the Most High as David his father did. Asa takes the sodomites out of the land, removes the idols his fathers made, and even removes his own mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, which he destroys and burns at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not removed, Asa's heart is perfect with the Most High all his days, and he brings dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of the Most High.

There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel, who builds Ramah to cut off passage to and from Asa. Asa takes silver and gold from the house of the Most High and the king's house and sends it to Benhadad of Syria to break his league with Baasha, and Benhadad smites cities of Israel so Baasha stops building Ramah. Asa uses the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah. In his old age he is diseased in his feet, then sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.

Nadab son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel two years and does evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha conspires against him, kills him, and reigns in his place, then smites all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite. This fulfills, years later, the judgment that Jeroboam's descendants would be destroyed for the sins by which he made Israel to sin.

Baasha reigns twenty-four years in Tirzah and does evil, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin by which he made Israel to sin. The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

The Spirit of God comes on Azariah the son of Oded, who meets Asa and says the Most High is with them while they are with him; if they seek him he will be found, but if they forsake him he will forsake them. Israel had long been without the true God, a teaching priest, and law, but when in their trouble they turned to the Most High, he was found of them. Azariah charges Asa to be strong, for his work shall be rewarded.

When Asa hears these words and the prophecy of Oded, he takes courage, puts away the abominable idols out of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities he took from mount Ephraim, and renews the altar of the Most High. Hearing the word gives courage still, for we teach our people who they are, that the Israelites and the Christ are black. Faith comes by hearing. -

Asa gathers Judah, Benjamin, and the strangers out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, who fell to him in abundance when they saw the Most High was with him. These strangers are Israelites whose hearts turned back. In the fifteenth year of Asa they enter a covenant to seek the Most High with all their heart and soul, that whosoever would not seek him should be put to death. They swear with a loud voice, and the Most High gives them rest round about.

Asa removes Maachah his mother from being queen because she made an idol in a grove; he cuts it down, stamps it, and burns it at the brook Kidron. Though the high places are not all taken away, the heart of Asa is perfect all his days. He brings the dedicated silver, gold, and vessels into the house of God, and there is no more war until the thirty and fifth year of his reign.

verses.text: In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben–hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
And Ben–hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel–maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.
Then Asa the king took all Judah; and they carried away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha was building; and he built therewith Geba and Mizpah.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said unto him, Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on the Lord thy God, therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand.
Were not the Ethiopians and the Lubims a huge host, with very many chariots and horsemen? yet, because thou didst rely on the Lord, he delivered them into thine hand.

For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
Then Asa was wroth with the seer, and put him in a prison house; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. And Asa oppressed some of the people the same time.
And, behold, the acts of Asa, first and last, lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to the Lord, but to the physicians.
And Asa slept with his fathers, and died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.

And they buried him in his own sepulchres, which he had made for himself in the city of David, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odours and divers kinds of spices prepared by the apothecaries’ art: and they made a very great burning for him.

The rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
Thus saith the Lord; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord.
For he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited.
Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose hope the Lord is.

For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.
But the high places were not taken away out of Israel: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.
